### Item 7 is the one I expect to fail

The generated formula is `<field>.asFile().<targetField>`. `asFile()` is real —
it resolves a Link to a File, confirmed in Obsidian's own source — but Bases only
registers these functions on a File: `asLink, hasLink, inFolder, hasTag,
hasProperty, linksTo`. None of them reads an arbitrary property.

If the column errors, Bases cannot read across a link and item 7 needs a
different mechanism entirely. It will only show on a schema with a **bound**
relation field; `Verse.Realm` is unbound, so nothing is emitted for it today.

### Disabling a plugin needs a restart

Removing `asset-renamer` from `community-plugins.json` does not unload a plugin
that is already running. Until Obsidian restarts, both the old plugin and the
merged one are live, each with its own ribbon icon — which is what produced a
`schema-mappings` source row during testing. After a restart the merged one
should show **`trait`** as the source and default the property to **`cover`**,
matching the schema's case rather than writing a second `Cover`.

## The branch model is half-built

Item 5 shipped the rules and the hook, but **no `data/<project>` branch exists**.

```bash
git checkout -b data/myproject
# remove the /data/ line from .gitignore on THIS branch only
git add -f data/
git commit -m "Track vault data on this branch"
```

`.githooks/pre-push` refuses any push of `data/` files to `main` or `feature/*`.
Enabled here; run `git config core.hooksPath .githooks` once per clone.

## Known gaps

- A schema renamed while one of its fields is unbound leaves that field's config
  note with a stale `configFor`; the orphan rule will flag it. The cleanup is
  manual and shows its reasoning, so a false positive is visible.
- `isRecordFile()` still treats `config/entity.md` as a record for backwards
  compatibility, though nothing generates it any more.
